dedupe_keys.name: osdu data platform the open group osdu forum open data platform and data definitions for energy subsurface wells and facilities

description: The OSDU Data Platform is an open, cloud-deployable data platform and data standard for the energy industry, first built for oil and gas subsurface and well data and extended to surface facilities and new energy. It is developed by The Open Group OSDU Forum, whose members include about 190 organisations, among them major oil operators and the four large cloud providers. Coverage: generic industry standard used worldwide. The platform bundles core, consumption and domain data management services, libraries and Airflow ingestion workflows released in milestones, with implementations for Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and IBM Red Hat OpenShift; the OSDU data definitions give standard entities, relationships and attributes for legal agreements, locations, organisations, process safety, wells, wellbores, completions, well equipment, geology, geophysics, reservoirs and surface and process facilities. Format and access: open-source code, APIs and schemas on the OSDU community GitLab, free of charge but behind account sign-in, with the data platform standard published by The Open Group. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): Apache-2.0 (OSDU community code). Caveats: the platform is heavy to deploy and aimed at operators' internal data, so it provides no public data itself. Simulation uses: a shared schema for asset inventories of wells, pipelines and process facilities used in digital twin and capacity planning work. Related records: the OGIM oil and gas infrastructure database (data-ogim-oil-gas-infrastructure-mapping) is public data of the kind OSDU models.
